newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward searching for retail CEO.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward searching for retail CEO.

text.p: Bernard Brennan, chairman and chief executive officer of Montgomery Ward Holding Corp. and its wholly owned retail unit, department store operator Montgomery Ward & Co., said Thursday the company has begun a search for a new chairman and CEO for the retail unit.
Brennan will remain as chairman of the parent company once a new retail chief of chosen.

Brennan is the largest individual shareholder of the company. He will retain his more than one-third ownership of the company and the right to three seats on the board of both the holding company and retail company.
Brennan said he sees the appointment of a new retail CEO as the next key step in the evolution of the company.

"We began the process with a major turnaround of our business in 1995, the largest management-led LBO in the country ($3.8 billion) in 1988, and the acquisition of Lechmere in 1994," Brennan said in a statement.

"There are other major efforts underway including a substantial refocusing and major redeployment of assets to branded apparel," he said. "While the early apparel transition transition has been difficult, we are beginning to see some very positive results," he added.

Brennan, 58, first joined Montgomery Ward in 1982 as executive vice president of store operations. In 1983, he left to become president and CEO of Household Merchandising, Inc. before returning to Montgomery Ward in 1985 as president and CEO.
In 1988, he led the $3.8 billion management buy-out of Montgomery Ward in partnership with General Electric Capital Corp.

Montgomery Ward, the largest privately held retailer in the United States, with annual sales exceeding $7 billion, operates 400 speciality stores in 43 states. It also is parent of Lechmere, an electronics retailer.
